notes:
Summary: enterprise contact-center SaaS vendor building AI agent assist and ticket automation for 1,500+ seat customers. Primary goal = spike reliability + predictable unit economics during incident bursts and seasonal peaks. Current stack: proprietary queuing layer, Postgres/Redis state, Twilio fronting. Wants Redwood as inference layer for suggestion generation, ticket summarization, and tool-calling orchestration.

Recent convo highlights:
- 'We need the model to not be the single point of failure during outages; degrade gracefully.' (VP Product)
- Prefers on-prem/VPC deployment for regulated customers, but will pilot hosted/dedicated for devcustomers.
- Heavy emphasis on deterministic fallbacks: cached completions, smaller local model, and prioritized routing.

Key technical asks (shorthand):
- Maintain median suggestion latency <250ms at baseline; tail latency 95th <600ms during 4x incident bursts.
- Sustained concurrency target: 1,200 concurrent agent sessions; peak burst: 4,800 requests/min (short windows).
- Request-level priority (supervisor/SA escalation) + queue backpressure indicators to throttle non-critical background summarization jobs.
- Tool-calling reliability: idempotent function-calls, replay-safe, observability for failed side-effects.
- Cost control: need guidance on batching + quantized model variants; want Optimize recommendations tied to real token distribution.

Security / compliance notes:
- Must support SSO/SAML, KMS for key management, audit logging for all inference calls, and data residency controls for EU customers.
- Infosec provided initial questionnaire on 2026-02-08; follow-up scheduled after POC.

Stakeholder quotes & flavor:
- AE note: 'Very pragmatic; will trade raw model quality for deterministic behavior under load.'
- Eng lead: 'If we can get predictable 95th psuedo-SLOs with autoburst reserved pools, this becomes a platform sale.'

Quick links & artifacts:
- Demo recording (fireflies): ff-20260220-vertex-demo
- Pricing draft in Drive: drive:vertex-pricing-draft-03-2026.pdf
- Security questionnaire thread: gmail-thread-CA9876asw-security

Sales posture: run 6-week POC -> load testing -> pilot with 3 customers (mid-May) -> procurement negotiation for reserved capacity and private deployment.

summary_requirements: Spike reliability first — must show graceful degradation (cached responses, fallback tiny-model) + prioritized queue backpressure. Latency SLOs 95th under burst. Function-calling idempotency and observability required for tool calls.
tech_preferences: Prefer GPU-backed dedicated pool for production; lightweight quantized local for offline fallback. Want model variants (gpt-style large -> distilled) and automatic routing/policy to shift to cheaper variants under load. Requires VPC/private control plane for regulated customers.
spike_reliability_requirements:
- Autoscaling with reserved burst capacity (configurable headroom)
- Traffic shaping: rate limits per agent + priority lanes
- Circuit-breaker + cached-prefix responses to keep agents online during model degradation
- Fallback routing across regions and model variants
- Load-test scenario: 4x baseline sustained for 10 minutes, 10x short spikes (30s)
- Clear cost-estimates for burst hours and recommended batching settings
